findings: The requirements doc (lines 9-13) says nothing about refunds at all — it only specifies status change to 'cancelled' and slot release — yet both implementations perform payment refund logic (`refund(booking.payment)`), so the actual refund behavior is entirely unspecified/undocumented.

The two implementations of the same operation diverge on refund eligibility: `api/cancelBooking.ts` (line 20) only refunds if `hoursUntil(booking.start) > 24`, while `admin/cancelBooking.ts` (line 29) refunds unconditionally on every cancellation, regardless of timing.

This divergence creates an exploitable/inequitable path: a customer cancelling less than 24 hours before their booking gets no refund via the self-service account page, but the identical cancellation performed by support staff via the admin panel always refunds — so a customer can bypass the cancellation-window policy simply by contacting support.

The 24-hour refund cutoff in `api/cancelBooking.ts` is a magic number with no corresponding requirement — there is no documented business rule stating what the refund window should be, so it's impossible to verify either implementation is 'correct'.
There is no requirement or code defining refund amount semantics (full refund vs. partial/fee-deducted refund), so `refund(booking.payment)` is ambiguous in both implementations.

Neither implementation guards against double-cancellation: calling `cancelBooking`/`adminCancelBooking` twice (e.g., duplicate request, retry after timeout) would call `refund()` a second time with no idempotency check, risking a double refund.

In both implementations, `booking.status = 'cancelled'` and `releaseSlot(booking.slot)` execute unconditionally before/regardless of the refund call, with no error handling shown around `refund()` — if the refund call fails (e.g., payment gateway error), the booking is already marked cancelled and the slot already released, leaving the system in an inconsistent state (cancelled + slot freed, but no refund issued) with no rollback or retry path.

Releasing the slot (`releaseSlot`) happens before/independent of refund completion in both paths, so the slot could be rebooked by another user while the original customer's refund is still pending or has failed, with no requirement addressing this race.

The admin implementation's unconditional refund could be an intentional support override (e.g., goodwill exception) or simply a bug/oversight — the requirements doc gives no indication either way, and there's no audit logging or authorization check shown in `adminCancelBooking` to record why a policy-deviating refund was issued.

The boundary condition `hoursUntil(booking.start) > 24` is strictly greater-than, so a cancellation at exactly 24 hours out is treated as within the no-refund window; this edge case is not specified in the requirements, so correctness of the boundary can't be confirmed.

There is no requirement or implementation detail describing what refund state is persisted on the booking/payment record (e.g., refund status, refund amount, refund timestamp), so downstream consumers (receipts, reporting, support tooling) have no defined data to rely on.
